name: Hafnarfjörður
title: Hafnarfjörður Thickness Measurement | Trawlers & Smelter Ships
description: Thickness gauging in Hafnarfjörður for trawlers, cargo ships and bulk carriers at the Straumsvík smelter: hull, hold and tank UTM, plus floating-dock work.
h1: Ultrasonic Hull Gauging for Fishing and Cargo Ships in Hafnarfjörður and Straumsvík
intro: Hafnarfjörður, just south of Reykjavík, is one of Iceland's largest fishing centres and its second-largest port for imports and exports. Trawlers land and refit here, container and general cargo ships work its quays, and bulk carriers bring raw materials to the aluminium smelter at nearby Straumsvík and load metal for export. The harbour's floating docks make it a repair base as well. Atlantis mobilises technicians from India to each ship, using dock periods and cargo stays as the gauging windows.

highlights.p: Bulk carriers delivering alumina to the Straumsvík smelter and loading aluminium for export lie alongside the smelter's own harbour during cargo work. Hatch covers, coamings, holds as they empty and ballast tanks can be gauged within that stay.

Hafnarfjörður's floating docks lift trawlers and smaller ships for maintenance, giving access to the shell, bottom, sea chests and stern area. A dock period is the natural time to measure plating that no afloat survey can reach.

highlights.h: A port close to the airport
highlights.p: Hafnarfjörður sits between Keflavík International Airport and Reykjavík, so the team can reach a ship soon after arriving in Iceland. That makes short jobs on cargo ships and landing trawlers practical even when the vessel's stay is brief.

port.h: Hafnarfjörður harbour and the Straumsvík smelter
p: Hafnarfjörður lies on the south side of the capital region, just beyond Reykjavík, at the natural harbour that gave the town its name, which means harbour fjord. Much of the town is built on an old lava field, and the harbour is protected by breakwaters and quays built out from the shore. It became a commercial port in the early twentieth century, when the first quay for large ships was built, and it has grown with the capital ever since, as a cargo port as well as a fishing harbour. North Atlantic weather reaches it fully in winter, and ships use the protected basins rather than anchoring off when conditions are poor, which is most of the time between autumn and spring.

Fishing remains central. Hafnarfjörður is one of Iceland's largest fishing centres, and the country's first fish auction market opened here; fresh-fish and freezer trawlers land catches, and fishing companies keep vessels based in the harbour. Freight has become the harbour's main business, with container and general cargo ships handling imports and exports for the capital region, and the town is Iceland's second-largest port for foreign trade. Just south of the town, the aluminium smelter at Straumsvík, Iceland's first, built at the end of the 1960s, has its own harbour, where bulk carriers discharge alumina and other raw materials and cargo ships load aluminium for export. The harbour's cargo and fishing quays lie close together, so a team on one job can reach another vessel without delay.

The town's floating docks add a repair dimension that most cargo ports lack. Icelandic trawlers and visiting fishing vessels are lifted for maintenance, hull painting and repair, and those periods are planned around the fishing calendar and each vessel's quota. Cargo ships come in on regular rotations and stay for as long as discharging and loading take, while the smelter's ships follow the plant's supply schedule. Small cruise ships also use the harbour in summer. In winter, short daylight and storms limit outside work, but work inside tanks, holds and machinery spaces carries on, and a docked hull can be measured from staging or the dock floor in calmer conditions than an exposed quay offers. Docking slots are booked well ahead by the fishing companies.

facilities.h: Gauging locations in Hafnarfjörður and Straumsvík
p: The floating docks are the place for the fullest gauging programmes in Hafnarfjörður. With a vessel lifted, the team can reach the shell from keel to waterline, the bottom plating, sea chests, rudder and stern frame, while internal tanks are opened at the same time by the crew or the repair company. For trawlers, that combines naturally with the fish hold, fuel tanks and trawl deck, so one docking produces a complete picture of the hull. The company operating the dock controls access, staging and lighting, and gauging is fitted into the repair programme so that steel renewal can be carried out before the vessel is floated out.

At the cargo quays, gauging is afloat work fitted into cargo operations: deck, hatch and container-guide areas, ballast tanks the crew has prepared and, on general cargo ships, holds as they are emptied. The Straumsvík harbour is a dedicated industrial berth inside the smelter's operating area, so any work aboard a bulk carrier there follows the plant's safety and access rules as well as the ship's own permits. Fishing vessels lying at the fishing quays between trips can be gauged without docking for a defined scope of holds, tanks and decks. Anchorage work off Hafnarfjörður is rarely realistic because of the weather, and almost all jobs are done alongside or in dock.
list: Floating docks — shell, bottom, sea-chest and stern-area gauging on trawlers and smaller ships lifted for maintenance.
Fishing quays — fish-hold, fuel-tank and trawl-deck readings on trawlers lying alongside between trips.
Cargo quays — deck, hatch and ballast-tank gauging on container and general cargo ships during their stay.
Straumsvík smelter harbour — hatch cover, coaming, hold and ballast-tank work on bulk carriers serving the smelter, within plant access rules.
Repair berths — afloat piping and structural checks on vessels under repairs that do not need a lift.

context.h: Iceland's rules, the smelter trade and the fishing fleet
p: Iceland is a member of the Paris MoU and of the EEA but not the EU, and it carries out port state control through the Icelandic Transport Authority. As an EEA state, Iceland applies the EU ETS to shipping along with other EU maritime measures, so ships trading between Hafnarfjörður and European ports report emissions much as they would within the EU. The smelter trade has its own pattern. Alumina is a dry, dusty cargo that demands tight hatch covers, so coamings, cover panels and their seals feature in condition checks alongside holds and ballast tanks. Where a bulk carrier serves the smelter repeatedly, the owner can plan gauging for a particular call well ahead.

For the fishing fleet, the governing framework is the Icelandic Transport Authority's rules for fishing vessels and the class rules where vessels are classed, rather than the ESP regime that covers tankers and bulk carriers. Under Iceland's quota system, vessels fish to allocated catch shares, and owners plan maintenance in the slack periods between quotas or seasons, which is when floating-dock time is booked. Freezer trawlers and fresh-fish trawlers have different weak points: the former carry refrigeration plants and processing decks on long trips, the latter make frequent landings with heavy use of fish holds and ice. Both benefit from readings taken at each docking, so that wastage trends are followed rather than discovered.

jobs.h: The gauging jobs we see in Hafnarfjörður
jobs.p: Hafnarfjörður work splits between docked fishing vessels, where the scope is a full hull and tank survey fitted into the repair period, and cargo ships at the quays or at Straumsvík, where it is a focused scope fitted into cargo operations. Fishing owners usually book us once their floating-dock slot is fixed, and expect daily results so that renewal can be agreed with the repair company while the vessel is still lifted. Cargo-ship requests come from superintendents preparing for a survey or responding to a recommendation. With Keflavík so close, short jobs on cargo ships are practical even when the ship stays only a day or two.
list: A fresh-fish trawler in floating dock: shell and bottom plating, sea chests and stern area gauged, with fish-hold and fuel-tank readings from inside.
A bulk carrier at Straumsvík discharging alumina: hatch covers, coamings and ballast tanks measured, and holds gauged as they are cleared.
A container ship at the cargo quays: ballast-tank and deck readings before its renewal survey at a European yard.
A freezer trawler alongside between trips: processing-deck plating and refrigeration piping UT, with MPI at gantry and winch foundations.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a second-hand trawler before it is bought into the Icelandic fleet.

logistics: Keflavík International Airport, on the Reykjanes peninsula, is closer to Hafnarfjörður than to Reykjavík, and the main road to the capital passes the Straumsvík smelter and the town. The team flies from India through a European hub and needs a Schengen visa, since Iceland is a Schengen state. Harbour access is arranged through the ship's agent or the vessel owner, floating-dock access through the repair company, and entry to Straumsvík through the smelter's own procedures.

faqs.q: Can bulk carriers be gauged at the Straumsvík smelter harbour?
faqs.a: Within the smelter's rules, yes. The berth sits inside an industrial site with its own safety and access requirements, so the team's details, induction and equipment are agreed through the ship's agent beforehand. Hatch covers, coamings, deck and ballast tanks can be measured during cargo work, and holds once they are clear of cargo and safe to enter.

faqs.q: Can a trawler be gauged while it is in a Hafnarfjörður floating dock?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is the best time for a complete survey. With the vessel lifted, the shell, bottom, sea chests, rudder and stern frame are accessible, and the crew or repair company can open internal tanks and holds at the same time. We coordinate with the dock operator so that readings are available before renewal decisions are taken and before the vessel is floated out.

faqs.q: How does Iceland's fishing calendar affect gauging?
faqs.a: Owners plan maintenance and docking for periods when their vessels are not fishing, often between quota periods or seasons, so the window is usually fixed by the owner months ahead. Once a dock slot or lay period is known, give us the dates and we plan visas and travel around them. Short jobs on trawlers alongside between trips are possible at shorter notice.

faqs.q: Is it possible to gauge ships at anchor off Hafnarfjörður?
faqs.a: Seldom. North Atlantic weather makes launch boarding unreliable for much of the year, and the harbour's sheltered quays and docks are almost always the better option. We plan Hafnarfjörður work alongside, in the floating docks or at Straumsvík, and if a ship cannot berth, the job moves to its next port of call.
